description.narrative: Stöd för kapacitetsutveckling av colombiansk polis, genom den svenska Polismyndigheten. Insatsen är en fortsättning på det samarbete mellan colombiansk polis och den svenska Polismyndigheten som har pågått sedan 2013. Projektet har utvecklats i samarbete mellan de båda myndigheterna och bidrar till reformen av Colombias säkerhetssektor, med fokus på ökad medborgerlig tillit och tillgång till polisens tjänster, samt med det övergripande målet att förbereda colombiansk polis för en framtida övergång från militär till civil myndighet. Genom insatsen har svensk polis en rådgivande funktion till sin colombianska motsvarighet, inom områdena polisutbildning, brottsförebyggande arbete och jämställdhet. Ingen vidareförmedling av medel sker till colombiansk polis inom ramarna för denna insats.

This is a project support for capacity development of the Colombian police, through the Swedish Police Authority. The aim is to prepare Colombian police for a future transition from a military to civilian authority. Through the contribution, the Swedish police have an advisory function to their Colombian counterpart, in the areas of police training, crime prevention and gender equality. The project has been developed in cooperation between the two authorities and contributes to the reform of Colombia’s security sector, focusing on increased civic trust and access to police services. The contribution is a continuation of the cooperation between the Colombian police and the Swedish Police Authority that has been ongoing since 2013, previous contribution ID-number: 52060048.

Support provided by the Swedish Police Authority for capacity development of Colombian National Police. The contribution is a continuation of the cooperation between the Colombian police and the Swedish Police Authority that has been ongoing since 2013. The project has been developed by the two police authorities and contributes to the efforts to make police-services more modern, efficient and accessible to the average citizen, with the overall goal of preparing the Colombian police for a future transition from a military to civilian authority, in the context of a stable and sustainable peace. Through the contribution, the Swedish police have an advisory function to their Colombian counterpart, in the areas of police-education, crime-prevention and internal gender equality. No forwarding of funds to Colombian police takes place within the framework of this contribution.

Example of results during project implementation
Preventive component
It was decided to implement the POLVE program nationwide. POLVE is a neighborhood surveillance program, oriented towards citizens, called "Policía de Vecindario". The project contributed to the design of the program and to the implementation and evaluation of the pilot study that formed the basis for the decision to implement the program nationwide. After its implementation in the pilot cities and an evaluation showing positive results, continued implementation focuses on areas most affected by the conflict - in line with Sida strategy objective 1.2 to strengthen conditions for peace consolidation and increase state institutional presence and capacity in conflict-affected areas.
Training component
With the approval of Law 2179, a new model for police teacher training and management was established, aimed at addressing societal challenges and needs more effectively. This decision also led to a revision of the curricula, which now includes subjects such as sexual violence, domestic violence, and crime prevention. Consequently, the law and updated curricula serve as guarantees for the ongoing focus and sustainability of these efforts. The SPA played a crucial role in shaping the reform and curricula by providing technical assistance, capacity building, guidance, benchmarking, and support to the CNP in both the development and implementation phases.
Gender equality
According to the final report, Colombian women are increasingly starting to see the police as a potential employer, female police officers are represented at all hierarchical levels and in different areas of the police service, which no longer limits them to performing only certain types of activities; similarly, men are being placed in units or positions that were only reserved for women and gender is no longer as important in appointing a professional to a position.
A final survey concluded that 87% of respondents believed that the CNP had made improvements in their efforts to enhance gender equality. However, only 68% of those identifying as LGBTIQ perceived the same level of improvement. 21% of women, 42.3% identifying as LGBTIQ, and 4% men reported experiencing sexual harassment. Additionally, 45% of respondents stated that sexual harassment is common within the CNP. These findings underscore the vulnerabilities faced by women, particularly those within the LGBTIQ community.
Resolution 03872 by which the Guidelines for Gender Mainstreaming in the Colombian National Police were adopted in 2021. The resolution was developed by the cooperation between SPA and CNP, together with CNP gender group.
Furthermore, through various training activities, the CNP's knowledge of gender issues was increased by training staff members at different levels and strategic key functions.
